_comment: Clan intrigue (docs/STORY.md 'Clans and trust'): Haus Marrovel, the Ruskwebers and the strangers from the map's edge. Favors and betrayals live in data/clans.json; ledger_* entries are the Ledger pages (first line = title).

lines: Wren: Welcome to the Crooked Kettle. Rooms by the night, secrets by the hour.
Wren: Two clans eat in my dining room. Haus Marrovel by the window, the Ruskwebers by the door.
Wren: Window, so they can be seen. Door, so they can leave fast. Tells you everything, really.
Wren: Marrovel keeps the old Rift pacts. The Ruskwebers keep everyone who works the mines.
Wren: My advice? Trust nobody who pays on time. That's a joke. Mostly.
Wren: Now. House rules. Everyone signs the guest book. Real name, if you've got one spare.
Wren: Tea's on the house. The house is very clear that it's on you, though.
Wren: Ilo Vash sold your blank battle record to the Ruskwebers.
Wren: Then he sold them a second copy. He calls it customer care.
Wren: A Ruskweber came asking for you by name. With a letter in Fenrick's hand.
Wren: I told him you'd died. He tipped me. Lovely man.
Wren: Corvane, is it? Write to me. And never sign your letters.
That night you spot Wren copying a page of her guest book into an envelope. Grey wax. Ruskweber grey.
The page with the name you made up. Somewhere a clerk is hunting a ghost with your handwriting.
Wren: Don't look at me like that, sweetheart. The Kettle has a roof. Roofs cost money.
That night you spot Wren copying a page of her guest book into an envelope. Grey wax. Ruskweber grey.
Your page. Your real name, neat as a gravestone.
Wren: Don't look at me like that, sweetheart. Mother Grell pays for every new face. Yours was new.
The Kettle's guest book
Wren sells a copy of every new page in her guest book to Mother Grell.
She calls it the rent that keeps the roof on. The roof has never leaked.
Pip: You're the map kid. Good. Maps don't gossip.
Pip: Last night I fought a Ruskweber Spirling at the Rift edge. Clan duels are banned.
Pip: Banned like sweets before dinner. Everyone does it, nobody gets caught. Until me.
Pip: It lost. Then it went silent, like the Hush took it, and walked into the Rift.
Pip: Its breeder ran in after it. Neither came out. Help me keep this quiet?
Pip: Choose fast, map kid. In this town a secret has the shelf life of milk.

choices.action: ledger ash; trust pip 15; trust vash 0 10; trust lipka 0 10
trust pip -20 10; trust fenrick -10; trust elma -15

lines: Pip: Someone slipped a note under my door that night. 'Duel at the Rift edge. Win.' No name.
Pip: The ink smelled of lavender. Nobody in my family wears lavender. Nobody admits it, anyway.
Pip: Grandfather smiles at me more lately. I don't like it.
Ash in the brooding oven
You burned the silent Spirling's things in a cold breeding oven, to hide Pip's duel.
The oven belongs to Ilo Vash's brother-in-law. Somebody swept up the ash and weighed it.
Marlo: Marlo, Spirling doctor. I mend legs, wings and the odd broken heart.
Marlo: What can I do for you?
Marlo: Again? Fine. You were here all night, holding a Puddlet's flipper.
Marlo: Every lie I tell for you costs something. I just don't know what yet.
Vash: Warden Ilo Vash, Clan Duels Office. Complaints are taken at noon.
Vash: The office closes at noon.
Vash: Don't make that face. Honest men starve in this valley. I have a very full face.
Vash: A blank battle record for Pip Kael's little evening? 300 coins.
Vash: Paperwork is a craft. Crafts cost money.
Vash: You reported a clan duel. To me. How refreshing.
Vash: I'll file it under 'sold'. Both clans pay well for honesty.
Vash: Your files are safe with me. Well. Your files are with me.
Vash: Pleasure. The record is blank. Spotless. Like my conscience.
Vash: The firewood for the oven is billed separately.
Vash: Pleasure. I sold a copy anyway, of course. But I left it blank.
Vash: Professional courtesy. Don't get used to it.
The blank battle record
Ilo Vash wrote nothing about Pip's duel, for money.
Then he sold the nothing to the Ruskwebers. Twice.
Fenrick: Fenrick Kael, head of Haus Marrovel. You may admire the portrait later.
Fenrick: It shows my Spirling. I'm in the corner. Modesty.
Fenrick: You helped my grandson. Family pays its debts, child. Usually with other people's coins.
Fenrick: Take this sealed letter to the ferry post. Do not read it. Reading is for clerks.
You break the seal. Fenrick's hand: 'The one who hid the duel is the map kid.'
He meant to hand you to the Ruskwebers. Postage paid.
You burn the letter. Somewhere a Ruskweber waits for post that never comes.
Fenrick: Lost in the mail? Pity. The mail is so unreliable these days.
Fenrick: No hard feelings, child. It was business. You were the cheapest thing in the room.
At the ferry post two Ruskweber hands are waiting. They know your face.
One of them grins. 'Fenrick says hello. He also says goodbye.'
Fenrick: Haus Marrovel never forgets a favour. We write them down. In ink.
Fenrick's sealed letter
Fenrick named you as the one who hid Pip's duel, and posted it to the Ruskwebers.
A scapegoat is cheaper than a son.
Aldra: You're staring. Yes, I came through the Wide Rift. Eleven of us did.
Aldra: The valley calls us the strangers from the map's edge. We call that rude.
Aldra: The clans hire us because nobody here owes us anything. Yet.
Aldra: Fenrick wants you to carry a letter? Read it first. Clans seal the true ones.
Aldra: Still breathing? Then my warning worked. Or Fenrick's aim is bad. Either way, you're welcome.
Aldra: Funny thing, though. Somebody paid me to warn you. Somebody with lavender on her gloves.
Aldra: Owing is the only honest thing in this valley. Everything else is a rumour with a price tag.
Aldra: Fenrick offered me forty coins to tell him you read his letter. I told him to post it himself.
Aldra: Don't get sentimental. Forty is an insult. Ask me again at a hundred.
Aldra: Fenrick offered me forty coins to tell him you read his letter.
Aldra: You called me a liar, so I took the coins. Fair's fair. Now he knows you know.
Aldra: Cheer up. Being hunted by a patriarch is basically a promotion around here.
Two warnings, one wage
Someone with lavender gloves paid Aldra to warn you about Fenrick's letter.
Fenrick offered her more to report that you read it. Whether she took it depended on you.
Lipka: Lipka, from beyond the edge. I sell tips. True ones cost extra.
Lipka: Lies are free. I'm practically a charity.
Lipka: Free sample: something rare sleeps behind the old mill tonight. Believe me?
Lipka: Tips are like weather. Mine are like weather in the mountains.
Behind the old mill nothing rare is sleeping. Two Ruskweber hands are wide awake.
One of them waves a paper. 'Lipka sends her regards. And her invoice.'
Behind the old mill: nothing. A tip can be honest and still be wrong.
Behind the old mill a small crate is waiting, with your name chalked on it.
Kenan: Kenan. Edge-born, Rift runner. The clans pay me to scout the Cinder Rift.
Kenan: My Spirling is hurt. Lend me your lead one for a single run? Back by dusk.
Kenan: Word of honour. I've got loads of it. Barely used.
Kenan: Rift runs are hard on keepsakes. Ask anyone.
Kenan comes back at dusk. Your Spirling looks fine. Lighter, somehow.
Kenan: The Rift was rough. Things fell off. Small things. Shiny things.
Kenan brings your Spirling back at dusk, tired and proud. Nothing is missing.
Kenan brings your Spirling back with a little gift from the Rift edge.
Nail: Nail. Edge-born. I'm opening a tea stall for the Rift workers.
Nail: I'm 200 coins short. I pay back with interest. Don't ask around. They'd lie.
Nail: Everyone lies here, mate. I just do it with a cup and saucer.
Nail: The tea is terrible. The Rift workers love it. Nobody understands business.
Nail: Your coins, plus interest. Don't look so shocked. Some of us are honest.
Nail: Your coins back. The interest went into the tea. You can taste it.
The tea stall is gone. So is Nail. A sign says 'Closed for honesty'.
Mother Grell: Mother Grell. I lead the Ruskwebers, since nobody else would.
Mother Grell: A Marrovel brat sent my best breeder into a Rift. I wear black now. It suits me.
Mother Grell: Don't flinch, little map. I don't hate children. I just invoice their families.
Mother Grell: Carry a warning to my apprentice in the Woadfen? You have an honest face. For now.
Mother Grell: Grief is a full-time job. I hire help.
Mother Grell: My apprentice left his hiding place after your warning. Marrovel blades were waiting.
Mother Grell: Strange how that works. I'll remember who carried it.
The mercy post
You carried Mother Grell's warning to her apprentice in the Woadfen.
The warning sent him out of hiding. Whoever waited there knew he would come.
Sable: Sable Ruskweber. Grell's nephew. The family's good side. I have two.
Sable: Aunt Grell grieves loudly. I grieve profitably. We all cope differently.
Sable: Friends tell each other things. So, friend: the Woadfen road is watched.
Sable: Take the reed path instead. Trust me?
The reed path is quiet. Under a stone you find a pouch tied with Ruskweber thread.
Sable was right. That should worry you more than it does.
The reed path is quiet. Sable was right. That should worry you.
The reed path is very quiet. Then it is full of Ruskweber hands.
Farida: Farida. Edge-born. I lodged at Wren's place in Veydal all last year.
Farida: Lovely woman. Never asks where her guests go at night.
Farida: She just writes it down. Habit. Like breathing, but with ink.
Farida: I'm 400 coins short for the ferry home. Help a fellow traveller?
Farida: Home is wherever the letters get paid for.
The ferry leaves without Farida. She was never going home. Your coins went to Mother Grell's post.
Farida pays you back the next morning, to the coin. She leaves no address.
Amir: Amir. Edge-born. I know eggs. Smuggled ones, mostly.
Amir: In Corvane even the eggs have alibis.
Amir: If Mother Grell sends anyone a gift, have it looked at. Eggs travel in odd places.
Amir: And Farida, by the crates? She writes to Mother Grell every night.
Amir: She paid Wren on time for a whole year. That should have been the clue.
amir_spy.action: ledger guest_spy; trust farida -10; betrayal wren_keys

lines: The spy in the guest book
Farida lived at Wren's guest house for a year and reported every guest to Mother Grell.
She always paid on time.
Brannoc: Brannoc Kael. Former Rift gladiator. Current disappointment.
Brannoc: Mother says I'm the heir. She says it the way people say 'the rash'.
Brannoc: Father wants the Woadfen routes drawn up. You're the map kid. Draw them for me?
Brannoc: I wanted out. Routes are a way out. Nobody said whose.
You draw the routes one bend wrong, as Elma said. The Ruskwebers who bought them end up in a bog.
Brannoc: The bog? That's... a very precise mistake.
On the Woadfen road the Ruskwebers know every bend you drew. Brannoc sold your map before the ink dried.
A Ruskweber hand taps your own map. 'Lovely linework. Shame about the artist.'
The Woadfen routes
You drew the Woadfen routes for Brannoc Kael. He passed them to the Ruskwebers.
He wanted money of his own, and a way out of the family.
Elma: Elma. Edge-born. I cook for the Kaels. Nobody else will, since the last feast.
Elma: Brannoc dined with a Ruskweber trader. The soup was excellent. Except for the guest.
Elma: Ottilie seasoned it herself. Brannoc had to watch. He hasn't been family since.
Elma: The trader left Corvane that night. Sleepy. Very sleepy. On a cart going nowhere nice.
Elma: If Brannoc asks you for routes, draw them one bend wrong. He sells them on.
The last feast
Brannoc bought Rift eggs behind the clan's back. Ottilie knew from the first egg.
The trader was the main course of the lesson, if not of the meal.
Heider: Heider. Edge-born. I sell news to both clans. Same price. I'm fair.
Heider: Fairness is my brand. Betrayal is just my delivery service.
Heider: Fresh one, free: Ottilie means to sacrifice one of her own Wardens. Believe it?
Heider: News goes stale fast. People don't. They just go missing.
The tip was true. Heider also sold the Ruskwebers the news that you believed it.
The tip was true. For once, Heider sold it to only one side.
Morrow: Warden Captain Dace Morrow. I investigate Haus Marrovel. Thoroughly.
Morrow: I also take Ottilie's coins. And Fenrick's. I keep two tills.
Morrow: The law is a scale, kid. I just make sure both sides pay to stand on it.
Ottilie: Ottilie Kael. The orphans call me Aunt. The Wardens call me Ma'am.
Ottilie: Fenrick calls me later. I'm always there later.
Ottilie: Lavender? Thank you, dear. I wear it to funerals. I go to a great many.
Ottilie: Mother Grell sent us a show Spirling as a peace gift. Lovely plumage.
Ottilie: And Captain Morrow rides out to the Root Rift on patrol tonight. Alone. Fenrick insisted.
Ottilie: The war? I ordered it, dear. Fenrick needed a war to look small in.
Ottilie: Write that in your little book. I keep a bigger one.
Ottilie: Speaking of your little book. Pip brought me something this morning.
Amir checks the show Spirling's feathers and finds a brood capsule full of spore fever.
Amir: Never look a gift Spirling in the beak? Always look. Twice.
That night the Marrovel stables burn with fever. A sick show Spirling breaks loose, wild with it.
The gift of honour
Mother Grell's peace gift carried a brood capsule of spore fever into the Marrovel stables.
You catch Morrow at the gate and tell him what Heider sold you. He leaves Corvane that night, with both tills.
Ottilie: Someone talked. How tiresome. I'll find out who. I always do.
News from the Woadfen: Captain Morrow had an accident in the Root Rift. He was a thorough man.
Ottilie: Fenrick's best Warden, gone. Fenrick will feel so very alone.
The Warden with two tills
Ottilie sent Captain Morrow, Fenrick's man, alone to the Root Rift to weaken her husband.
The ordered war
The clan war was no accident. Ottilie ordered it, to bring down her own husband.
Someone sent Pip to that duel. The ink was hers.
Ottilie opens her hand. Ash. Fine grey ash, the kind a cold breeding oven makes.
Ottilie: Pip copied your Ledger for me, then burned the copy on my doorstep. The child has manners after all.
Ottilie: Loyalty to a stranger. How very expensive of him. I'll send him the bill.
Ottilie opens a stack of pages. Your Ledger, every entry, copied out in Pip's round handwriting.
Ottilie: You reported his duel, dear. He reported you. Children learn so fast.
Ottilie: He wanted a smile from his grandmother. I gave him two. They were free.
The copied Ledger
Pip copied your Ledger for Ottilie. What he did with the copy depended on what you did with his duel.
Amir: One more thing. Farida's last letter to Grell had a second note folded inside.
Amir: Wren's hand. 'The kid is mine. Sell anyone else. W.' Grell burned it. I didn't.
Amir: One more thing. Farida's last letter to Grell had a wax impression folded inside.
Amir: A room key. Your room at the Crooked Kettle. Wren cut it when Ottilie threatened the roof.
Amir: Don't take it personally. Landladies have one true love, and it's the building.
The spare key
Ottilie threatened the Crooked Kettle. Wren had to decide whose secrets were worth a roof.
How far she trusted you decided whether your room key went into Farida's post.
Vash: Chief Warden Vash now. Both clans backed me. Each thinks I'm theirs.
Vash: New rule: Rift duels need a permit. Permits cost money. I love rules.
Sable: Old friend! You look terrible. Ashmere suits you.
Sable: There's a card hall under the basalt. Friends only. Small stakes, big snacks.
Sable: Bring your strongest Spirling. Card halls get rowdy. Somebody always flips a table.

sable_after: Sable: Nothing personal. It was a business decision. You were the business.
Sable: No hard feelings? I've got some soft ones. Cheap. For you.
sable_struck: Under the basalt there are no cards. Only Marrovel's enemies, a price list, and your name on it.
Sable: I said friends only. They're my friends. You're the snacks.
Sable: Don't look at me like that. I gave you a discount. Forty percent. That's practically love.
sable_caught: You come in through the coal chute, behind the ambush. Six hands turn round at once.
Sable: Ah. You read the room. I hate it when people read.
Sable: For the record, I was going to warn you. Right after they paid. Timing is everything.

lines: The card hall
Sable Ruskweber invited you to a card hall as a friend and sold you to the highest bidder.
Mirza: Mirza. Edge-born. I play cards with Sable. I lose on purpose. It pays.
Mirza: Stake me 300 coins tonight? I win, you win.
Mirza: Cards are honest. It's the players you have to watch.
Mirza: We won. Your share, plus mine, minus nothing. Don't tell anyone I'm generous.
Mirza: And if Sable invites you to his card hall: there are no cards. Use the coal chute.
Mirza: We broke even. Your stake, back. Now a free tip.
Mirza: If Sable invites you to his card hall: there are no cards. Use the coal chute.
Mirza lost your stake. On purpose, he says. It paid. Just not you.
Leith: Leith. Edge-born. I run errands for Sable.
Leith: Tip for free: the basalt shortcut to the Kiln Rift is safe now. Believe me?
Leith: ...Sable did. He's selling you at his card hall. I never said that.
Leith: Nobody sent me. I just like you. Everybody likes you.
Leith: Errands, errands. Somebody has to carry the bad news.
The basalt shortcut is not safe. It is full of people Sable owes favours.
The basalt shortcut really is safe. Leith looks almost as surprised as you.
Marlo: Ashmere air is terrible for wings. Business is booming.
Marlo: Clan people asked me where you were the night of Pip's duel.
Marlo: I said: with me. They didn't like that answer. I may need to lie low.

marlo_lives: That night masked hands come for Marlo. He is busy setting a Shalebat's wing.
Marlo: Rude of them to wait. I made them hold the bandage. They left with clean hands.
Marlo: They asked me to swear on my mother's name. I said she charges extra.
marlo_gone: In the morning Marlo's clinic stands open. His bag sits by the spring, still packed.
On the counter: a bill for your last three alibis. Marked 'paid in full'.
Someone paid for the lies he told for you. The Ledger doesn't say who.

lines: The alibi
Marlo swore you were with him the night of Pip's duel. Every time you asked.
An alibi is a debt that the alibi pays.
Lejla: Lejla. Edge-born. I copy documents. Sometimes the copies are better.
Lejla: Pip asked me to read the old Kael breeding registers. Look at the bond seals.
Lejla: Pip's seal matches Fenrick's line. Not Brannoc's. Fenrick is her father.
Lejla: Fenrick's new daughter, Liss? She has me copy her letters. All addressed to Sable. Lovely hand.
Lejla: And Leith? He talks to people he trusts. I told him you're dull. He trusts dull.
The seal in the breeding register
Pip's bond seal matches Fenrick's line, not Brannoc's. Fenrick is her father.
Pip: Lejla is reading the old registers for me. Don't tell anyone. Especially family.
Pip: I thought I had his eyes. They were someone else's.
Pip: And the note that sent me to that duel? Same ink as Grandmother's letters.
Brannoc: Ashmere. Nobody here knows my name. I could get used to that.
Brannoc: So Pip is Father's. And I was the cover story. I'm done with Marrovel.
Brannoc: Thirty years I was the heir. Turns out I was the wrapping paper.
Brannoc: The Ruskwebers offered me work. Fixed hours. No family dinners. I said yes before they finished.
Mother Grell: You again. Alive. Sable must be losing his touch.
Mother Grell: My breeder? He's fine. Under the station, counting eggs.
Mother Grell: Grief was cheaper than a war. And it paid much better.
Mother Grell: I wore black for a month. Black is slimming. Everybody won.
Mother Grell: Now you know. Knowing is expensive, dear. Who are you going to sell it to?
The breeder who lived
Mother Grell's breeder never died in the Rift. She hid him and staged her grief.
Fenrick: My bond seal is fading. Some nights my Spirling forgets whose side it is on.
Fenrick: Some nights so do I. Ottilie says it's my age. Ottilie says many things.
Fenrick: Also, I have a daughter. Liss. From Ashmere. Long story. Short evening.
Fenrick: Ottilie gave her a room by the stairs. Ottilie always gives people rooms by the stairs.
The hands take what they came for and leave you by the road. Nothing personal.
Sable: A friend? Bring two. The more the merrier. The more the cheaper per head.
Sable: ...That came out wrong. It's the ash. Makes a man honest at the worst moments.

liss_caught: At the family dinner Liss passes you the salt, and a folded note under the table. You keep both.
The note is for Sable. It lists every word said at the council. Including 'pass the salt'.
Liss: ...Fine. Sable pays me. Fenrick only pays attention. Which would you pick?
From now on she writes what you tell her. Fenrick never forgives you for knowing first.
liss_struck: Liss smiles all through dinner. By dessert Sable knows the Marrovel convoy route.
Liss: Welcome to the family. The food taster sits on the left. I sit wherever the money is.
On the road out of town, Ruskweber hands are waiting. They brought a map. Yours.

lines: Fenrick: Do you hear them? My old Spirlings. They want their supper. They've been gone for years. Still hungry.
Fenrick's bond Spirling turns its head towards you. Its eyes are somewhere else. Some other century.

fenrick_after3: Fenrick: He's not wicked. He just mixes up the centuries. So do I, after lunch.
seal_caught: Marlo is already there, sleeve rolled up, sleeping draught in hand.
Marlo: Big lad. Little sip. Sleep it off, both of you.
Fenrick: I will remember this humiliation. ...What was I remembering?
seal_struck: Nobody comes. You run. The Spirling runs faster, and snatches your lead Spirling's keepsake as a trophy.
Fenrick: Terribly sorry. He's never liked cartographers. Neither have I, but I have manners.
ledger_liss: Liss Arden, Fenrick's daughter, reports every Marrovel council to Sable.
ledger_seal: Fenrick's bond seal is failing. His Spirling turned on you. Ottilie knew and said nothing.

lines: Vash: Chief Warden Vash, on holiday. Holidays are when I do my best paperwork.
Vash: Big day. We're draining the old basin under the sun palace. Civic hygiene.
Vash: Funny what turns up at the bottom of things. Want to watch?

vash_4_after: Vash: Water forgets nothing. It has that in common with accountants. And me.
basin_caught: The basin drains. At the bottom: sand, one boot, and nothing with your name on it.
Vash: Where is it? There was... I mean. Good. Clean. Very clean. Well done, everybody.
Up on the cemetery wall, Tobs waves his shovel. He charges by the scoop.
basin_struck: At the bottom of the basin lies a Marrovel-sealed urn: the ash from the brooding oven. Veydal sends its regards.
Vash: Every name in your Ledger is a witness now. Half of them have already sold their statement.
Vash: The other half are on their way. Wardens! Arrest this person. Gently. Paperwork hates bruises.
ledger_basin: Vash moved the brooding oven ash to Solenne and drained the basin in front of witnesses.

lines: Tobs: Vash's men buried an urn in the palace basin last month. Marrovel seal. Heavy for ash.
Tobs: I could move it tonight. Five hundred coins. Shovels don't sharpen themselves.

choices.text: What are your rates for silence?

lines: Tobs: Silence is free. Everybody here is quiet eventually. I just help with the timing.
Tobs: You asked nicely. I like that. Nobody asks a gravedigger anything nicely.

tobs_4_after: Tobs: Sand's easy to dig. Harder to keep shut.
tobs_reward: Tobs: Done. The urn sleeps under the old cistern now. And here: you overpaid. I'm a gravedigger, not a thief.
tobs_kept: Tobs: Done. The urn sleeps under the old cistern now. Don't visit. It gets attached.
tobs_betray: Tobs takes your coins, then takes Vash's coins to tell him you paid. Business is steady in Ochrewell.

lines: Ottilie: Sit, dear. Solenne is so warm. People drop like flies. Purely the heat, of course.
Ottilie: Fenrick is fading. The clan needs a steady hand. Yours, at my side. The pact deeds, too.
Ottilie: Just sign. The wax is still warm. I warmed it myself.

choices.text: Let Marlo look at the wax

wax_marlo: Marlo sniffs the seal. Then he sniffs it again, the way he sniffs a bad tooth.
Marlo: Sleepwort in the wax. Lick the seal and you nap for a week. Or for good. Depends on the week.
Marlo: Fenrick buys his wax from the same shop. I'd ask him about his, too.

lines: Fenrick: Ah, my favourite scapegoat! No, no, I mean that warmly.
Fenrick: Ottilie wants my chair. Let's give it to you instead. A son in all but blood and paperwork.
Fenrick: The pact deeds, the clan, the portrait wall. Sign here. Mind the wax, it's my own recipe.

fenrick_4_late: Fenrick: The sun's set on Solenne, they say. Then it rises again, the show-off.

lines: You tell Fenrick about Ottilie's offer. Then you tell Ottilie about Fenrick's. Same wax, same smile.
By sunset they are not speaking. By midnight they are writing to their lawyers. By morning the deeds are in your bag.
Two offers, one sleepwort. At least they agree on something.
deeds_play.action: trust ottilie -40; trust fenrick -40; ledger deeds

throne_o_caught: You hand the contract back unsigned. The wax is green. Wax is never green.
Ottilie: Clever. I do so hate clever. It always lives longer than planned.
throne_o_struck: You seal the contract the old way, with a lick of wax. The room tilts gently into the sand.
Ottilie: Sleep, dear. The clan will be in such good hands. Mine.
You wake behind the bazaar, coins gone, guards circling. The heat, of course.
throne_f_caught: You blow on the seal instead of licking it. Fenrick watches the green smoke curl and sighs.
Fenrick: Ottilie's recipe. I stole it. Forty years of marriage, and that's what we share.
throne_f_struck: The wax tastes of honey and bad decisions. Then of nothing at all.
Fenrick: No hard feelings! I'll have your portrait painted. Lying down. Very restful.
ledger_throne: Ottilie and Fenrick each offered you the clan seat. Both seals carried the same sleepwort.
ledger_deeds: You played the Kaels against each other and walked off with the Rift pact deeds. Neither will forgive it.

lines: Wren: Surprise. I took the sand road. Ottilie wants the Crooked Kettle as an egg store. Contraband eggs.
Wren: She says you'll talk me round. Will you?

choices.action: set_flag c4_wren_chose; trust wren -70; trust ottilie 15
set_flag c4_wren_chose; trust wren 20; trust ottilie -20

wren_4_left: Wren: Right. Then I'll leave you the key. And the cellar. Mind the cellar.
Wren: There's a Ruskweber spy down there. Been there since spring. He's learned to knit. Feed him Tuesdays.
wren_4_kept: Wren: Good answer. Wrong for your health, but good.
Wren: I tidied the cellar. There's a Ruskweber spy down there since spring. He knits now. Lovely scarves.
Wren: Ottilie won't like this. Ottilie doesn't like weather either, and it still happens.

lines: Wren: Rooms by the night, secrets by the hour. In Solenne, the hour is shorter.
Wren looks through you, as if you were a guest who never paid.
Mother Grell: Solenne. Our second seat. Here the sand keeps our secrets. Usually.
